solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diamonds, for example, in small case

parts.note: minor means small or lesser
a suit is a legal case brought in court, as in lawsuit

explanation.surface: Jewels kept in a little box or bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' looks like gems in a jewellery case, but here it is the card suit; in bridge diamonds and clubs are the lower-ranking suits.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, diamonds is one of the two lower-ranking card suits, so it is an example of the term.

clue.text: Female teacher with anxiety on motorway?

indicators.note: in a down clue the motorway sits above, so its letters come first

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
stress is anxiety or strain

explanation.surface: A worried woman teacher stuck in traffic on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress is the old-fashioned British word for a woman schoolteacher, as in the maths mistress.

clue.text: Catch neighbour attempting burglary, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: first letter of neighbour
first letter of attempting
first letter of burglary

explanation.surface: Catching the next-door resident in the act of trying to break in.
explanation.definitionFit: Nab is informal for seize or arrest, as police do to a suspect.

clue.text: Backflipping in dare, dirt bike user

indicators.note: backflipping means the hidden letters are turned to read backwards
in signals that the letters sit inside the words dare and dirt

parts.note: the letters span the end of dare and the start of dirt

explanation.surface: A daredevil stunt on a dirt bike, flipping backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds REDIR across 'dare, dirt', and 'Backflipping' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone who rides a motorcycle or bicycle, the person on the saddle.

clue.text: Latest finished item out, then reordered

parts.note: up can mean finished, as in time's up

indicators.note: reordered means these letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A shop sold out of something, so it was put on order again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished' gives UP, as in 'your time is up'; 'reordered' then rearranges ITEMOUTTHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-the-minute is an idiom for the most recent or current, as with news or fashion.

clue.text: Row with caterer in a frenzy

indicators.note: being in a frenzy means wildly agitated, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An argument with a frantic catering worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel with the caterer, but it means a line of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a common type of British street housing.

clue.text: Face attack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a person's face
second meaning: to assault and rob someone in the street

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings of one short word: the slang noun for a face and the verb for a street robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a person's countenance and also means to set upon and rob a victim.

clue.text: Vegetable lover, scram!

parts.note: a woman's man is her lover or partner
scram is a command meaning get out

explanation.surface: Someone shouting at their boyfriend to clear off, or at a greengrocer's item.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a flat pea pod eaten whole, its French name meaning eat all; in the US it is a snow pea.

clue.text: Joy in middle of night having hauled up fish

indicators.note: middle of means take the central letter of the word night
in a down clue, hauled up means the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: An angler's delight at landing a catch in the dead of night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives G, the centre of NIGHT; 'hauled up' turns EEL into LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is a noun for great delight or merriment.

clue.text: Wrong bit used, correct on paper

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic fitted the wrong drill bit, and the mistake was put right in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to check and correct written copy before it is printed, an editorial job on a newspaper.

clue.text: Wash off a little toddler in sea

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A parent cleans a small child who has been paddling in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it lightly with clean water, removing dirt or soap.

clue.text: Turning device that spins both ways?

indicators.note: spinning both ways hints that the word reads identically from either end

parts.note: a rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades

explanation.surface: A gadget that can rotate clockwise or anticlockwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke: the device turns, and the word itself 'spins both ways' because it is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades or an engine's spinning component.

clue.text: Actor with little time reading a novel

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performer with only a short while to read a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book to read, but as an adjective meaning new it rearranges READINGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles on stage.

clue.text: River the same, not entirely different

indicators.note: different tells us the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
not entirely means the phrase loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A paradox: a river that is the same yet partly different, as in never stepping into the same river twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts the last E from THE SAME, leaving THESAM, and 'different' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river flowing through London, the best-known river in England.

clue.text: Press top after twisting plugs

indicators.note: twisting means the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions on a bottle: push the lid down, then twist to seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppers are bungs or corks that seal the neck of a bottle, as plugs do.

clue.text: Barry, for example, sees red as riot breaks out

indicators.note: breaks out suggests the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man called Barry loses his temper as public disorder erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry looks like a man's name, but it is a town in south Wales with a beach at Barry Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry, on the south Wales coast, is a holiday town by the beach, an example of this kind of place.

clue.text: Something that floats, leaves

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mass of ice drifting in the sea
second meaning: ... lettuce, a salad of crisp leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb for departing; here it is lettuce leaves, from the iceberg variety.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a drifting block of ice, and it is also a crisp variety of lettuce used in salads.

clue.text: From Western Asia, you chaps and I

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A travel note saying you, some fellows and I come from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen lies at the south of the Arabian Peninsula in West Asia, so this adjective describes something from there.

clue.text: Leaders in uniform trounced in competition, very upset

indicators.note: in means the leading letters are placed inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition with a trophy, such as the FA Cup

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: first letter of uniform
first letter of trounced

explanation.surface: A team in uniform is heavily beaten in a tournament and left distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' gives U and T, and 'in' places them inside CUP after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is British informal for deeply distressed, as in being cut up about bad news.

clue.text: Price covering a cruise

indicators.note: covering means the price word wraps around the letter a

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: The fare that pays for a holiday at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruise' looks like a noun for a sea holiday, but it is the verb: to coast is to move along without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move smoothly with little effort, as a car or cyclist freewheels; cruising is the same.

clue.text: Mark wants knitted garment shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the garment loses its last letter

parts.note: a scarf is often a knitted woollen garment

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark asks for a jumper to be taken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is a blemish left on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting blemish left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Country I left, claimed by revolutionary

indicators.note: claimed by means the letters are taken inside the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A traveller's country is taken over by a rebel leader after they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE is Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary; I and L go inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a long, narrow nation on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Different nail hammered into small instrument

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the instrument

parts.note: a uke is a ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar

indicators.note: hammered means the word nail is battered into a new shape

explanation.surface: A nail driven into a ukulele, a strange thing to do to an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A uke is the short name for the ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar from Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalike is a synonym meaning dissimilar, not resembling each other.

clue.text: Primarily, indignation about fury

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of indignation
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Mostly it is indignation that lies behind rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger or wrath.

clue.text: Manage race

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be in charge of, as in running a business
second meaning: a race on foot, or to go fast

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings of one short word: to be in charge of something, and a quick sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: You run a company when you direct it, and a run is also a contest of speed on foot.

clue.text: Sergeants built for glory

indicators.note: built suggests the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Army sergeants are made for honour and fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory and greatness are both nouns for eminence and distinction earned through achievement.
